1. Platform Overview

BeeMonitor is a cloud-based platform for automated monitoring of solitary bee nesting activity. It uses computer vision (YOLO object detection) to detect bees, wasps, and nests in video footage, track their movements, and classify entry/exit events at nest tubes.

Key Capabilities:

  • Upload and manage field video recordings
  • Automated bee/wasp detection and tracking using GPU-accelerated AI
  • Entry/exit event classification at nest tubes
  • Visual analytics: hourly, daily, monthly activity patterns
  • Nest activity heatmaps (6x10 grid)
  • Annotation tools for labeling and reviewing detections
  • Custom model training to improve detection for your specific sites
  • Batch processing of multiple videos in parallel
  • Export data as CSV for further analysis

3. Uploading Videos

Navigate to Videos in the top menu, then click Upload Videos.

Direct Upload

  1. Click "Upload Videos" on the Videos page
  2. Select one or more .mp4 video files from your device
  3. Videos are uploaded to Azure cloud storage
  4. Once status shows "Ready", they can be analyzed

Video Naming Convention

For best results, name your videos with the pattern:

sitename_YYYY-MM-DD_HH_MM_SS.mp4

Example: meadow_east_2024-06-07_12_30_00.mp4

BeeMonitor automatically extracts the site name, date, and time from the filename for filtering and analytics.

Filtering Videos

Use the filter bar at the top of the Videos page to filter by site, year, month, or day.

4. Connecting Video Sources (S3)

If your field cameras upload directly to Amazon S3, you can connect BeeMonitor to your S3 bucket.

  1. Go to Sources in the menu
  2. Click "Add Source" and enter your S3 credentials (Access Key, Secret Key, Bucket, Region)
  3. BeeMonitor will list available videos from your bucket
  4. Select videos to import — they are automatically transferred to Azure for processing

Note: Credentials are encrypted at rest using Fernet symmetric encryption. BeeMonitor never stores plaintext credentials.

5. Analyzing Videos

Batch Analysis (Recommended)

  1. Go to Videos page
  2. Filter videos by site/date if needed
  3. Use "Select All Filtered" or check individual videos
  4. Click "Customize" to adjust analysis settings (optional)
  5. Click Analyze Selected

Analysis Configuration

Setting Default Description
GPU TierA10GGPU type. A10G is the best balance of speed and cost.
Confidence0.25Detection threshold (lower = more detections, more false positives).
Two-Mode TrackingEnabledUses motion detection + YOLO (faster). Disable for YOLO every frame.
Annotated VideoGenerateCreates a video with detection boxes drawn. Skip to save time.
Nest Detection ModelBuilt-inSelect a custom-trained nest detection model.
Bee Tracking ModelBuilt-inSelect a custom-trained bee/wasp tracking model.

Presets

  • Fast (~200 credits/video): T4 GPU, higher confidence, no annotated video
  • Standard (~350 credits/video): A10G GPU, default settings
  • Quality (~400 credits/video): A10G GPU, lower confidence threshold

Deduplication

BeeMonitor automatically skips videos that have already been analyzed with the same configuration. This prevents duplicate processing and wasted credits.

6. Viewing Results & Analytics

Go to Analytics to see all your results.

Job Progress Tracker

At the top of the Analytics page, you'll see a progress bar showing processing, completed, and failed jobs. The page auto-refreshes every 30 seconds while jobs are running.

Summary Cards

Overview statistics: total videos analyzed, total events detected, average events per video, unique tracks, entries, and exits.

Charts

  • Cumulative Activity: Running total of events over time
  • Hourly Activity: Average events by hour of day (entries vs exits)
  • Daily Activity: Average events by day of week
  • Monthly Trend: Activity pattern across months
  • Nest Heatmap: 6x10 grid showing which nests are most active

Data Export

Download combined data across all completed jobs:

  • Events CSV: All entry/exit events with timestamps, nest IDs, and track IDs
  • Tracking CSV: Raw tracking data with frame-by-frame positions

Individual Job Results

Click "Results" on any completed job to see per-video details: annotated video playback, events table, tracking data, and statistics.

7. Annotation Projects

Annotations let you label objects in video frames to create training data for custom models.

Creating a Project

  1. Go to Annotate → New Project
  2. Enter a name, description, and class labels (e.g., "bee, wasp, nest")
  3. Click Create

Adding Videos

  1. On the project page, click + Add Videos
  2. Filter by site if needed, select videos, click Add

AI Pre-annotation

Click AI Pre-annotate All to automatically detect objects in all project videos using YOLO. This creates initial annotations that you can then review and correct.

  • Samples frames every 10 frames (~3 per second)
  • Runs YOLO detection on each sampled frame
  • Saves detected bounding boxes as annotations
  • Extracts and saves frame images for fast viewing
  • Takes 1-4 minutes per video

Reviewing & Editing Annotations

The project page shows all annotated frames in a visual grid. Click any frame to open the annotation editor.

  • Prev/Next Frame: Navigate through all annotated frames across all videos
  • Arrow keys: Left/Right for quick navigation
  • Draw boxes: Click and drag on the frame to create a bounding box
  • Select class: Choose the active class (bee, wasp, nest) before drawing
  • Delete boxes: Click "Del" next to any box in the sidebar
  • Save: Click "Save Annotations" to persist your changes

Exporting Dataset

Click Export Dataset to download a YOLO-format ZIP file containing:

  • data.yaml: Dataset configuration with class names
  • images/train/ and images/val/: Frame images (80/20 split)
  • labels/train/ and labels/val/: YOLO-format label files

8. Training Custom Models

Fine-tune YOLO models on your annotated data to improve detection accuracy for your specific sites and species.

Starting a Training Job

  1. Go to Training → New Training Job
  2. Select an annotation project (must have annotated frames)
  3. Choose a base model:
    • YOLOv8n (Nano) — fastest, smallest
    • YOLOv8s (Small) — better accuracy
    • YOLOv8m (Medium) — best accuracy, slower
  4. Set epochs (default 50), image size (640), batch size (16)
  5. Click Create — training runs on an A10G GPU

Training Metrics

After training completes, you'll see:

Metric Description Good Value
mAP50Mean Average Precision at 50% IoU> 0.7
mAP50-95mAP averaged across IoU thresholds> 0.5
PrecisionOf all detections, how many are correct> 0.8
RecallOf all actual objects, how many are detected> 0.6

Uploading Pre-trained Models

You can also upload a YOLO .pt model file directly:

  1. Go to Training → Custom Models → Upload Model
  2. Enter a name and select the model type:
    • Nest Detection — appears in the Nest Detection Model dropdown
    • Bee Tracking — appears in the Bee Tracking Model dropdown
    • Custom — appears in both dropdowns
  3. Upload the .pt file and optionally specify class names

9. Using Custom Models for Analysis

Once you have a trained or uploaded custom model, you can use it for analysis:

  1. Go to the Videos page
  2. Click Customize to expand the analysis configuration
  3. Under Nest Detection Model, select your custom nest model
  4. Under Bee Tracking Model, select your custom bee model
  5. Select videos and click Analyze Selected

Tip: You can use a custom model for one task (e.g., nest detection) and the default for the other (e.g., bee tracking). The two models are independent — nest detection and bee tracking may have different taxonomies.

10. Credits & Usage

BeeMonitor uses a credit system to track GPU usage. 1 credit = 1 second of GPU time.

Credit Costs

Activity Typical Cost
Video analysis (10-min video)~350 credits on A10G
AI Pre-annotation (per video)~30-60 credits
Model training (50 epochs)~300-500 credits

Free Tier

Every account starts with 3,000 credits per month (enough for ~8-10 video analyses). Credits reset monthly.

Checking Usage

Click your username in the top-right corner to view your Usage & Credits page with detailed breakdowns by GPU tier and monthly trends.

11. Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What video formats are supported?

MP4 is the primary supported format. Videos should be recorded at a fixed camera angle pointing at the nest box.

Q: How long does analysis take?

A 10-minute video typically takes 3-6 minutes to process on an A10G GPU, depending on the amount of activity.

Q: My analysis job failed. What should I do?

Check the error message on the Analytics page. Common issues: video file is corrupted, S3 credentials expired, or insufficient credits. You can re-submit the job.

Q: How many annotations do I need for training?

For decent results, aim for at least 200-500 annotated frames with diverse examples. More annotations generally lead to better model performance.

Q: Can I use my own YOLO model?

Yes. Go to Training → Custom Models → Upload Model. Upload any .pt YOLO weights file and specify whether it's for nest detection or bee tracking.

Q: What species does BeeMonitor detect?

The default models are trained on solitary bees (primarily mason bees and leafcutter bees), wasps, and nest tube entrances. You can train custom models for other species or taxonomy.
